title: Anomalous regularization of passive scalars up to the Obukhov–Corrsin exponent
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of S. Armstrong and V. Vicol, "Anomalous regularization of passive scalars up to the Obukhov–Corrsin exponent" (2026, included as doc/paper.pdf). The velocity field b is constructed as in Armstrong and Vicol, "Anomalous diffusion by fractal homogenization": a bounded, Z^2-periodic, divergence-free field on R x T^2, built from shear flows alternating in direction at infinitely many scales, Hölder continuous in space and time with exponent alpha < 1/3, with its scale separation parameter q taken close to 1 depending on s. For the advection-diffusion equation d_t theta + b . grad theta = kappa Laplacian theta on T^2 and every s < (1 - alpha)/2, with b built for that s, it proves: the solutions are bounded at positive times in C^{0,s}(T^2) by C times the L^2 norm of the initial datum, uniformly in kappa in a union of bands accumulating at zero (Theorem A); every solution dissipates a fixed fraction of its variance in unit time, and the variance decays exponentially, with constants independent of kappa in the bands, of the L^2 datum and of the initial time (Theorem B); the local form of Theorem A in space-time tubes that follow the flow of the coarse velocity fields, without boundary conditions (Theorem C); and the compactness of the solutions as kappa tends to zero in the bands, with limits that solve the transport equation and satisfy the bounds of Theorems A and C (Corollary D). It also contains every statement of Part I of the paper.
